thread.title: 3 Things to Know at Market Close: Wild Week for the Markets

author: Katherine Ross
title: 3 Things to Know at Market Close: Wild Week for the Markets
text:
It's almost Friday!
Let's sum up what happened today so that we can all take a breather and prepare for tomorrow.
U.S. markets were having trouble sustaining momentum from Wednesday's record breaking session with all three major indices falling sharply shortly after the opening bell Thursday, December 27. After declining sharply for most of Thursday's session all three major indices closed trading in the green.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.14%, or 260 points to 23,139, while the S&P 500 rose 0.85% and the Nasdaq rose 0.38% .
FAANG's Toothless Or so reports TheStreet's Tony Owusu .
FAANG stocks failed to build on their big rally on Wednesday, as the majority of tech stocks fell sharply amid a market downturn on Thursday.
At the close, Facebook Inc. ( FB ) shares were up slightly, while Amazon Inc. ( AMZN ) shares closed down 0.6%, Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) shares also declined 0.6%, Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) shares were up 0.7%, and Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ) shares were up nearly 0.5%.
FAANG had an extremely strong session on Wednesday , with all five stocks posting increases more than 6%. But Thursday's session did not have the same ring to it, as the tech giants resumed their woes of the last several weeks.
Nvidia's Fallin' TheStreet contributor Rob Lenihan reported on what caused the chip giant to fall on Thursday.
Shares of Nvidia Corp. NVDA slipped almost 1.5% to $131.17 Thursday morning after RBC Capital lowered its price target on the graphics chip maker's stock to $200 per share from $230.
Analyst Mitch Steves said in a note to investors that average selling prices have been coming down in secondary markets. RBC still rates the stock "outperform."
Steves wrote that ASPs have decreased over the past month, which he thinks is due to additional secondary market sales. Focusing on Nvidia's GTX gaming graphics processing unit, Steves said "as this is a gaming chip, Nvidia is unlikely able to discern if sales are for pure gaming purposes or crypto currency mining."
"When we look at the price trends, we notice a slight downward move that aligns with our belief that sales could be a bit more muted in the month of December," Steves said. "While this is likely a near-term issue and doesn't impact the long-term story, we think it is prudent to remain conservative for next quarter."
Steves said Nvidia recently ramped up its efforts within the automotive segment.
"Beyond the addition of sensors and connected devices," Steves said, "we note that display technology should also increase in the future, which creates the need for more computing power. This can include upgraded navigation systems, back-seat passenger displays, and surround-view technology."
20 Tech Predictions TheStreet's Eric Jhonsa is making a list and checking it twice.
Just kidding. But he is making a list of tech predictions that he has going into 2019.
"Here's the first half of a set of predictions on what the new year will deliver for both tech giants and smaller peers. As a rule, I tried not to get carried away here (e.g., I'm not predicting Amazon will buy Walmart, or that Apple will snap up Disney)," wrote Jhonsa. "As well as to learn from what I got right and wrong when making predictions at the end of 2016 and the end of 2017 ."
While it's important to read what Jhonsa himself has to say, here's a rundown of his predictions.
Facebook versus Google Chip and software firms are looking to consolidate AWS will sign more enterprise deals Snap's SNAP gonna explore its options Waymo takes the lead Might be time for the Apple car The beginning of 5G Accelerated computing as the rule, not the exception. Google's possible cloud acquisitions Curiosity isn't sated? You can find Jhonsa's predictions part one here and his second part here .
Whew. Catch y'all tomorrow.
